title: Bhrigu's Kick
hookLine: a sage kicks Vishnu in the chest, and Vishnu answers the person, not the kick: Vaisheshika's six kinds of thing
carry: the person is substance; moods and acts pass
tomorrow: Drona asks his students what they see. why does only Arjuna pass?
last: THE UNSEEN HOLDS UP THE BANYAN.

cards: The sages have a question they can't settle, and they send the sage Bhrigu to test the gods. When he reaches Vishnu, he finds him resting, with Lakshmi beside him. Bhrigu doesn't bow.
He walks up and kicks Vishnu in the chest. Everyone waits for the anger. Vishnu rises, bows to Bhrigu and says, in the Bhagavata's telling: welcome, please sit, forgive us for not seeing you come.
Your feet are so tender. And he takes the sage's foot in his hands.

teach.h: KSHAMA, AND SIX KINDS OF THING.
teach.b: Bhrigu goes back to the sages amazed, and tells them what he saw. The story is often told for Vishnu's kshama, forbearance, which the Manusmriti counts among the ten marks of dharma.
And you can read it through today's school. Vaisheshika names the kinds of thing that exist: padarthas, whatever a word can name and the mind can know. Its Sutra lists six.
First, substance, dravya: the thing that holds the rest. Bhrigu himself. Second, quality, guna: a color, a weight, a mood.
Bhrigu's rudeness. Third, action, karma, which here simply means motion. The kick.
Fourth, the universal, samanya: what all sages share. Fifth, particularity, vishesha: what makes Bhrigu this sage and no other.
Sixth, inherence, samavaya: the glue that holds a quality in its thing, the way red belongs in a ripe mango. Later writers in the school added a seventh: absence. Here's the teaching, plainly.
A quality comes and goes, and an action is over once it's done; the substance is what holds them.
Vishnu answered the substance. He met the sage, not the rudeness, and not the kick. That's a reading, not the Bhagavata's own words, but it's why this list is more than filing boxes.
At home, someone you love snaps at you.
The person is the substance. The irritation is a quality, and it passes. The snapping is an action, and it's already over.

teach.h: MEET THE PERSON, NOT THE KICK.
teach.b: When you can see the seams, the snap doesn't have to become the whole person.

how: Students of Vaisheshika learn its list of categories, the padarthas, at the start of their study, and later Nyaya-Vaisheshika primers teach the list with absence added as a seventh.

o: the school that names the kinds of thing there are
a list of the gods who rule over each element
a rule for sorting good deeds from bad ones

games.q: Bhrigu's kick, in kinds of thing — tap the pairs.
p: the red belonging in the mango

s: Vishnu struck back when Bhrigu kicked him
he rose, welcomed the sage and took his foot in his hands.
in Vaisheshika's list, karma means fate
in the categories, karma means action: motion, like a kick or a falling mango.
later writers in the school added absence as a seventh category
the empty place is real too.

games.q: your dad snaps at you after a long day. by Vaisheshika's list and Vishnu's answer, what's in front of you?
o: a snappy person: one sharp act shows who he always is.
a person, a passing mood, and an action that's already over.
a mood that has taken over the person.
games.why: the person is substance; irritation is a quality that comes and goes; the snap is an action, done. Vishnu met the sage, not the kick.

practice: Look at something in front of you, a cup, a plant, your own hand, and name the substance, one quality and any action. Then let someone who snapped at you recently come to mind.

Name the person, the mood and what they did, and notice how the mood and the act pass while the person stays. If you pray, hold that person, not their mood, before God, the way Vishnu met the sage and not the kick.
If you don't, just say their name kindly.

wordCard.voice: Vaisheshika. A school that names the kinds of thing in the world: substance, quality, action, the universal, the particular, inherence, and later, absence.

orig.note: Sanskrit: padartha, explained as the meaning of a word: whatever a word can name.

carryVoice: Your line: the person is substance; moods and acts pass. Vishnu asked after the foot. See you tomorrow.
